deep.reconstruction:
This page is not mathematical research. It is a teaching outline for an elementary physics lecture: section III of a course on mechanics of fluids. The previous page covered hydrostatics of liquids: pressure at a horizontal level, specific gravity, balloons, the hydraulic press, absolute vs. relative pressure.

(a) Heading: 'III Ausdehnsame Flüssigkeiten' – expansible fluids, i.e. gases. A line follows introducing the concept by means of the parts (particles) and the behaviour of gases. Its wording is only partly legible.

(b) Main law: Boyle–Mariotte. The first statement reads roughly: 'Änderung (Steigerung?) der Druckkraft : Änderung der zugehörigen Volumina = const.' In modern form this is p·V = const at fixed temperature, equivalently p ∝ 1/V. Riemann then strikes out a version and restates it via density. Density is defined as 'Zahl der Lufttheilchen in demselben Raumtheile', the number of air particles per unit volume, ρ = N/V. The law becomes 'Dichtigkeitsänderungen gleich Druckänderungen': density changes in the same ratio as pressure, p/ρ = const, i.e. p₁/p₂ = ρ₁/ρ₂. He labels it '(Mariotte)', with a marginal note 'Anwendung' / 'Ableitung'.

Implicit step (mine): with fixed mass m, ρ = m/V. Hence p·V = const is equivalent to p/ρ = const.

(c) Applications/consequences, numbered:
1) The pressure of the free atmospheric air, apparently acting on all masses ('alle Massen').
2) Measuring pressure ('Druckmesser', manometers). Pressure is related to density, i.e. the law is used to infer density from pressure. The barometer is used for determining the atmospheric pressure ('Barometer zur Bestimmung derselben').

The page ends with a reference to experiments ('Versuche') on the pressure and a struck-out line. No derivation is carried out on the page.
errors: No mathematical errors; the statements are qualitative or proportional forms of Boyle–Mariotte's law, stated correctly (implicitly at constant temperature, which is not mentioned on the page).

The opening ratio statement ('...der Druckkraft : ...der zugehörigen Volumina = const') must, to be correct, be read as an inverse proportion (p·V = const), not a direct ratio of pressure to volume. The illegible first word likely encodes this. The density formulation that follows (pressure ∝ density) is correct.

results.what: At constant temperature the pressure of a gas is proportional to its density (pV = const)
Density defined as number of particles per unit volume; barometer/manometer as pressure measurement

deep.surprise_reason: Elementary lecture outline on gases (Boyle–Mariotte law, barometer), standard 19th-century textbook physics; only of minor biographical interest as evidence of Riemann's elementary physics teaching notes.

checkable.sympy: m,V1,V2,p1=symbols('m V1 V2 p1',positive=True); p2=p1*V1/V2; simplify(p1/(m/V1) - p2/(m/V2))
checkable.asserts: If p1*V1 = p2*V2 (Boyle), then p/rho is constant with rho = m/V (result 0).

checkable.sympy: p1,p2,rho1=symbols('p1 p2 rho1',positive=True); rho2=rho1*p2/p1; simplify(rho2/rho1 - p2/p1)
checkable.asserts: Density changes in the same ratio as pressure (result 0).

transcription_corrections: Line 2 likely reads something like 'd. Begriff klar durch Theile u. d. gas. Wahrnehmung/Wesen' – uncertain; the machine reading is plausible but not certain.
In the line beginning 'I.' the first word is not clearly 'Dichtigkeit'. It is more likely 'Änderung' or 'Steigerung' (der Druckkraft : ... der zugehörigen Volumina = const. od.).
'in derselben Raumtheile' is better read as 'in demselben Raumtheile'.
'Dichtigkeitsänderungen gleich Druckänderungen' probably reads 'Dichtigkeitsänderungen gleich[en/gemäß] Druckänderungen' (proportionality).
'Ableitung[?]' under '(Mariotte)' may be 'Anwendung'/'Ableitung'; the line after '(Mariotte)' reads 'Anwendg.' or similar.
Item 1 ends with what may be 'regieren' or 'regulieren' before 'alle Massen'.
'Druckmessen' is more likely 'Druckmesser' (manometer) in both occurrences.
